Ukraine-wide transport disruptions as new checkpoints spark economic slowdowns

KYIV, Ukraine (June 26) — A sweeping expansion of military checkpoints across Ukraine has disrupted economic activity nationwide, snarling logistics networks and slowing trade as authorities respond to heightened security threats amid the ongoing armed conflict in the east.

The Ukrainian Interior Ministry said Wednesday that more than 120 new checkpoints had been established in the past three days on major highways, regional routes and urban entry points. Officials cited concerns about potential sabotage and arms smuggling as conflict intensified near Kharkiv and Dnipro. “We are acting to ensure the safety of our citizens and critical infrastructure,” ministry spokesperson Oleksandr Kovalchuk said at a televised briefing.

The new measures have triggered major delays for freight haulers and delivery services. Nova Poshta LLC, Ukraine’s leading parcel delivery company, reported that deliveries across several regions were running up to 48 hours behind schedule. “We understand the importance of security, but these disruptions are having a significant impact on our operations and our clients,” said Nova Poshta spokesperson Iryna Melnyk.

The Ukrainian Union of Entrepreneurs estimates the combined effect of checkpoint delays and curfews could cut daily commercial activity by as much as 25% in affected districts. “Businesses across sectors—from food suppliers to manufacturers—are struggling to get goods to market,” union president Serhiy Bondarenko said.

The National Bank of Ukraine has urged businesses to prepare for continued volatility. “We expect logistical challenges to persist as long as the security situation remains fluid,” central bank analyst Kateryna Savchenko told reporters. Authorities have not indicated when or if the intensified checkpoint regime might be eased.
